page: Amazon Web Services r6idn.xlarge is a memory-optimized Nitro-based virtual server designed for memory-intensive workloads that require fast local scratch storage and consistent network performance. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon Platinum 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz, providing 4 vCPUs derived from 2 dedicated physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The configuration includes 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, offering an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio (8.0 GB per vCPU). In addition to its compute and memory layout, the instance comes provisioned with a 237 GB NVMe SSD for direct local storage and provides a 6 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. No dedicated GPUs are included in this profile.

Benchmark results highlight solid single-thread performance paired with throughput constraints consistent with its 4 vCPU count. In single-threaded operations, the server delivers balanced results, achieving a Geekbench single-core score of 1,625.0 and an encryption score of 3,617.55 on PassMark, supported by hardware cryptographic extensions including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. CPU instruction set extensions also support AVX-512 vector acceleration. Multi-threaded testing reflects the physical boundary of two execution cores, generating a PassMark CPU score of 5,830.61 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 3,448.0. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 28.95 GB/sec, while write operations peak at 25.21 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency and architecture perspective, the r6idn.xlarge trades off broad parallel compute power for high memory density and localized I/O performance. Because it integrates attached NVMe SSD storage and dedicated 6 Gbps networking directly into the instance profile, it mitigates latency compared to remote network block storage for temporary data operations. The instance is suited for workloads that require high RAM capacity and low-latency local caching without demanding high multi-threaded core counts, such as in-memory caches, small-to-midsize relational databases, static web serving, and localized data processing pipelines.

Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with x86_64 architecture, it delivers 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory at a high 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The configuration integrates 237 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps, operating without a discrete GPU.
